title: Resolve console 'time warp' in per-model usage splits caused by delayed shard replays
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Symptoms: Console per-model breakdown charts show apparent drops and increases (a 'time warp' effect) when ingest latency spikes or late shard replays occur. Root visible problems include duplicate token counts for some model aliases, short-lived incorrect quota bucket consumption, and transient per-model percentage shifts. This ticket consolidates investigation, a deterministic fix for attribution during late/backfilled events, and a conservative rollout that avoids disrupting billing while restoring chart correctness.
reproduction_steps: 1) Seed a small test tenant with streaming/standard requests across model aliases (m-small, m-large).
2) Stop the real-time ingest to the aggregator for ~20 minutes to simulate a shard outage.
3) Replay the buffered shard events via the backfill path with original event timestamps preserved.
4) Observe console per-model charts and quota consumption for the affected window — expect double-counting or shifted totals during replay window.
5) Run the reconciliation job with --dry-run to inspect adjustments reported by the correction pipeline.
technical_findings: Delayed shard replay preserves event timestamps but the merging pipeline currently merges by ingest_time then remaps to model_alias which can double-count when the same request is re-emitted from multiple shards.
Quota bucketing uses sliding windows keyed by ingest_time causing events with older event_time but newer ingest_time to be applied to the wrong billing window.

Per-model percentage computation relies on rolling aggregates that are not idempotent across backfill runs — lack of event provenance causes charts to show transient inflation before the backfill reconciliation job runs.
Rate-limiter accounting (token buckets) emits late correction metrics that are currently not surfaced to console, leading to apparent quota overages without visibility.
proposed_solution: 1) Make ingestion deduplication deterministic by using canonical request_id + event_time as the idempotency key at the merge layer.
2) Change quota bucketing to align by event_time (with a configurable drift allowance) instead of ingest_time, with a safety flag to avoid retroactive billing changes for customers.
3) Introduce a 'backfill provenance' marker on reconstructed events so console rendering can choose to show provisional vs reconciled totals.
4) Emit a paired correction metric when reconciliation changes aggregates, and add a delta line to console charts to show corrections for transparency.

5) Add integration tests and a staged rollout: dry-run reconciliation -> reconciliation in a read-only observability cluster -> opt-in customer during pilot -> full rollout guarded by monitoring alerts.
rollout_plan: Phase A (dry-run, internal): deploy dedupe and event_time bucketing to staging; run reconciliation with dry-run on last 30 days; validate deltas < 0.5% across tenants.
Phase B (observability cluster): enable actual reconciliation but mark corrections as 'provisional' in console; monitor correction_rate, chart divergence, and billing pipeline health for 72 hours.
Phase C (pilot customers): opt-in list of 10 low-risk customers with dedicated support; run full reconciliation and collect feedback.
Phase D (full): enable by default with opt-out and add automated rollback if correction spike > 2% or customer support tickets rise beyond threshold.
monitoring_queries: 1) SQL: SELECT model_alias, sum(tokens) FROM usage_events WHERE event_time BETWEEN $start AND $end GROUP BY model_alias;
2) SQL: SELECT ingest_shard, count(*) FROM ingestion_log WHERE replayed = true AND event_time BETWEEN $start AND $end GROUP BY ingest_shard;

notes: 2026-03-03: Initial triage by Aisha and Liam. Confirmed reproduction on staging with synthetic shard outage.
2026-03-05: Spike in late replays seen after autoscaler test; created synthetic load to validate dedupe approach.
2026-03-07: Design review with PM Sofia Martinez; agreed on showing provisional corrections rather than mutating historical billed totals.
2026-03-09: Security reviewed dedupe keys and found no PII exposure; security signoff by Rahul Verma.
2026-03-10: PR #2147 merged to staging; started dry-run reconciliation against last 14 days.
2026-03-12: Dry-run results: median correction per-tenant 0.12%, 99th percentile 1.8% for tenants with high replay rates. Proceed to Phase B with observability cluster.
Reviewers: Priya Shah (metrics), Diego Alvarez (quota), Nora Kim (console).

Risk: Retroactive billing changes are unacceptable; solution must avoid changing paid invoices. We will therefore only surface corrections in console and schedule billing-facing reconciliations as separate, customer-notified batches if needed.
Follow-ups: create ENG subtask for customer communications templates and support runbook.
